unsupported_claims: Edge sampling uses alias tables, so each sample costs O(1) after O(|E|) preprocessing (alias table is not in the provided evidence)
The vertex-side negative sampling table adds O(|V|) memory (not in the evidence)
Training first-order and second-order models separately and concatenating them doubles the constant factor but keeps the same order (not stated in the evidence)
K is the number of negative samples per edge and d the embedding dimension (not defined in the provided evidence)
rationale: The core claim O(dK|E|), linear in edges and independent of |V|, is directly supported. The extra details on alias tables, memory, the doubled constant factor, and the definitions of K and d are not in the provided evidence, although they are plausible from the original paper.
